problemStatement:
Problem Statement: Visually impaired people face difficulty detecting obstacles and knowing their direction and distance while walking. Conventional mobility aids may not provide immediate directional feedback.
Hardware Solution: Wearable ultrasonic glasses use two ultrasonic sensors to detect obstacles in front-left and front-right regions. An Arduino Nano calculates real-time distance and controls two buzzers, producing side-specific and distance-based sound alerts. The system is powered by a 9V battery and designed to be lightweight and hands-free.
Innovation: The system combines real-time sensing, directional warning, synchronized central alerts, and distance-based beep patterns in a low-cost wearable device, enabling safer and intuitive navigation for users.
